The [[Nonpartisan blanket primary|top-two primary]] was held on August 6. Incumbent [[Washington State Democratic Party|Democratic]] Governor [[Jay Inslee]] was eligible to seek a fourth term but decided that he would not do so.{{Cite web |last=Furtado |first=David |date=May 1, 2023 |title=Governor Inslee announces he will not seek re-election |url=https://keprtv.com/news/local/governor-inslee-announces-he-will-no-seek-re-election |access-date=May 1, 2023 |publisher=KEPR |language=en}} The Democratic candidate, state Attorney General [[Bob Ferguson (politician)|Bob Ferguson]], defeated the [[Washington State Republican Party|Republican]] candidate, former Congressman [[Dave Reichert]], who conceded defeat on November 19. Ferguson defeated Reichert with 55.51% of the vote in the general election. He also became the first Democrat to win [[Clallam County, Washington|Clallam County]] since [[2000 Washington gubernatorial election|2000]]. This election marked the 11th consecutive victory of the Democratic candidate for governor of Washington. Washington has not had a Republican governor since [[John Spellman]] left office in 1985,{{cite web | url=https://captainstack.medium.com/the-candidates-running-to-be-washingtons-next-governor-61869c44f17a | title=The candidates running to be Washington's next governor | date=February 17, 2024 }} the longest streak of Democratic leadership of any state in the country and the third-longest streak of one-party leadership after [[South Dakota]] (which has not had a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor since [[Harvey Wollman]] left office in 1979) and [[Utah]] (which has not had a Democratic governor since [[Scott M. Matheson|Scott Matheson]] left office nine days prior to Spellman in 1985).{{cite news |last1=Wood |first1=Benjamin |date=July 19, 2019 |title=Zachary Moses, a Democratic candidate for governor, wants to break up Republican control of Utah and build a space port |url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2019/07/19/zachary-moses-democratic/ |access-date=August 29, 2019 |work=Salt Lake Tribune}}{{cite news |last1=Scott |first1=Dylan |date=November 7, 2018 |title=Kristi Noem elected first woman governor of South Dakota |url=https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2018/11/7/18055928/midterm-election-results-south-dakota-governor-kristi-noem-winner |access-date=August 26, 2019 |work=Vox}}{{cite news |last1=Camden |first1=Jim |date=January 16, 2018 |title=John Spellman, Washington's last Republican governor, dies |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/jan/16/former-gov-spellman-dies/ |access-date=August 23, 2019 |newspaper=The Spokesman-Review}} == Primary election == Washington is one of two states that holds a [[top-two primary]], meaning that all candidates are listed on the same ballot regardless of party affiliation, and the top two advance to the general election. The filing deadline was May 10, 2024. On that day, two candidates named Bob Ferguson entered the race at the behest of a conservative activist who sought people with the same surname as [[Washington Attorney General]] [[Bob Ferguson (politician)|Bob Ferguson]], who was considered the Democratic frontrunner.{{cite news |last=Withycombe |first=Claire |date=May 10, 2024 |title=Three Bob Night: Two more Bob Fergusons running for WA governor |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/politics/three-bob-night-two-more-bob-fergusons-running-for-wa-governor/ |work=The Seattle Times |accessdate=May 14, 2024}} The two new candidates—a retired state employee and a [[U.S. Army]] veteran—resigned from the race on May 13, the deadline to withdraw, after questions about the legality of their campaigns arose. Washington's state statutes prohibit a new candidate with the same surname as an already-filed candidate from running with the intent to confuse or mislead voters.{{cite news |last=Withycombe
